bullets.text: CR was 94.6 compared to 89.5 prior year, with February topping 98. Operating with less safety net against the aggregate calendar-year 96 goal presents both a challenge and an opportunity.

Executed over 80 product/state rate revisions in Q1. Earned premium per vehicle fell 5–6% across most products and closer to 9% in Commercial Auto, with net rate increases taken to meet loss cost inflation.
Personal Lines written premium fell 4% and earned fell 3% YOY; Agency written and earned lagged prior year by 6% and 5%; Direct was essentially flat; Commercial Auto premium declined.
PIF grew 1% in Personal Auto, 8% in Special Lines, and 6% in Commercial Auto. Agency and Direct PLE rose ~9% and ~11%, reaching mid-2006 highs in most tiers; named most improved in ACSI.

Total investment return was negative 2% fully taxable equivalent. Unrealized gains fell over $500 million since year-end 2007. Progressive recognized $50.2 million in OTTI losses and remains comfortable with preferred stock and mortgage-backed allocations.

Agency personal auto PIF fell 2% (representing ~62% of total), while Direct grew 7% (~38% of total); Internet remains fastest-growing Personal Auto segment; Massachusetts entry planned via Direct first.

Appointed Larry Bloomenkranz Chief Marketing Officer and launched a thematic television campaign. Progressive partnered with the X PRIZE Foundation to fund a $10 million prize for 100 mpg vehicles that can be produced commercially.

Announced May entry into Massachusetts' $4 billion market via Direct first. Lifted some restrictions on segments of concern in NY and CA Personal Auto; slowed FL and CA Commercial Auto growth to ensure profitability.

Estimating loss cost inflation and the flow of rate revisions into earned premium are critically important. Progressive prefers acting early with rate changes, retaining the ability to adjust if severity trends moderate.

Margins approaching acceptable thresholds across the industry will create a new feel to competition. Pricing skills and speed to react will be at a premium, and Progressive feels well suited to compete.
